results.content:
For voters searching for who's winning the midterms right now, the answer remains the same:

Republicans likely hold a slight edge, but control of Congress is still very much up for grabs.

## Who will win the 2026 midterm elections? Polls, predictions and odds

According to the latest RealClearPolling' generic Congressional voting polls, 48.6% said they'd vote Democrat, 41.5% said they'd vote Republican. [...] In the latest generic congressional voting poll by Economist/YouGov, 40% said if elections for Congress were being held today, they'd vote for the Democratic candidate compared to 32% that said Republican. A whopping 29% said other, not sure or that they would not vote at all.

results.title: New Marquette Law School Poll national survey finds inflation and cost of living the most important issue; economy next most important

results.content:
The Democrats’ lead over Republicans in an average of national polls on the generic congressional ballot stands at 6.4 points, the same as on August 3. The high point so far for Democrats in 2026 was a lead of 7.1 points.  

August brought Republicans some good news as gas prices leveled out. The average price for a gallon of gas today stands at $4.09, which is down a penny from last month and is substantially lower than the peak average of roughly $4.50 a gallon earlier this year.
